In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of network positioning systems is strongly influenced by the number and the distribution of the FSs, by the signal-to-noise ratios of the measurements, and by the presence of biased measurements.

network-based positioning systems can achieve very high positioning accuracy, provided that the number of FSs is not small and the nuisance effects are minimized.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in spite of the fact that the positioning performance of a cellular system is highly dependent on the environment in which it operates, it is also highly dependent on the system-design parameters.

a network-based positioning system should be designed to minimize the effects of the following parameters: (a) the number of FSs used to estimate the position, (b) the number of signal paths from the FSs to the MS, (c) the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), (d) the MS's distance from the FSs, and (e) the FS's azimuthal orientation relative to the MS.
